notes.front: What is a data warehouse?
notes.back: A relational database whose schema is optimised for data analytics rather than transactional workloads.
notes.explanation: Data from transactional stores is reshaped into that analytical schema before it is queried.
notes.example: Like a shop’s year-end ledger, rearranged so totals by month and product are easy to read, unlike the till roll.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Data warehouses
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a data lake?
notes.back: A file store, usually on a distributed file system, holding data for analysis.
notes.explanation: Engines such as Apache Spark run queries over the stored files to return data for reporting.
notes.example: Like a huge shared drive of logs, images and exports, kept as files until someone analyses them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Data lakes
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is schema-on-read?
notes.back: Defining a tabular schema for data files at the moment they are read for analysis, not when they are stored.
notes.explanation: No constraints are applied at write time, so varied files can land in the lake as they are.
notes.example: Like keeping receipts loose in a box and only sorting them into columns when you do your tax return.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Data lakes
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a data lakehouse?
notes.back: A hybrid that combines data lake and data warehouse features: files in a lake, queried as tables with SQL.
notes.explanation: Raw files stay in the lake while a SQL layer exposes them as tables.
notes.example: Like a library that keeps every book on open shelves but also offers a catalogue you can search by author and title.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Hybrid approaches
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Apache Spark?
notes.back: A data processing engine that splits work across a cluster of machines so very large data is processed in parallel.
notes.explanation: It handles both batch processing and stream processing, in Python, Scala or Java.
notes.example: Like dividing a million exam scripts among a hundred markers who work at the same time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore Apache Spark structured streaming”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Delta Lake?
notes.back: A table format that improves the performance and reliability of lake data; the default format in a Fabric lakehouse.
notes.explanation: Data loaded into a Fabric lakehouse is stored in this format without extra setup.
notes.example: Like adding a ledger to a filing room, so every change to the files is recorded and half-finished edits never show.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “Lakehouse and Delta Lake tables”, What are Delta Lake tables?
notes.evidence: When you store data in a Fabric Lakehouse, data is stored as Delta Lake by default. Delta Lake adds capabilities that improve both performance and reliability

notes.front: What is medallion architecture?
notes.back: A design pattern that organises lakehouse data into bronze, silver and gold layers of rising quality.
notes.explanation: It is the recommended design approach for Fabric, implemented by creating lakehouses in OneLake.
notes.example: Like a recycling plant: mixed waste arrives, gets sorted and cleaned, and leaves as ready-to-use material.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “Understand medallion architecture for Fabric with OneLake”, Overview
notes.evidence: is a design pattern that's used to organize data in a lakehouse. It's the recommended design approach for Fabric. Since OneLake is the data lake for Fabric, medallion architecture is implemented by creating lakehouses in OneLake. Use this article after you choose medallion architecture to plan its implementation, including layer design, deployment models, storage formats

notes.front: What is Microsoft Fabric?
notes.back: An analytics platform for end-to-end data work, from ingestion and transformation to real-time processing, analytics and reporting.
notes.explanation: Its experiences, such as Data Engineering, Data Factory and Data Warehouse, share one compute and storage model.
notes.example: Like a single office building where the post room, workshop, archive and boardroom all share one lift and one filing system.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Microsoft Fabric?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Microsoft Fabric is an analytics platform that supports end‑to‑end data workflows, including data ingestion, transformation, real‑time stream processing, analytics, and reporting. It provides integrated experiences such as Data Engineering, Data Factory, Data Science, Real‑Time Intelligence, Data Warehouse, and Databases, which operate over a shared compute and storage model.

notes.front: What is OneLake?
notes.back: The unified data lake that every Microsoft Fabric tenant includes: the single place for the organisation’s analytics data.
notes.explanation: It is a central repository to store, manage and govern data for analytics and AI workloads.
notes.example: Like one company-wide network drive that every department uses, instead of each keeping its own.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is OneLake?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Microsoft OneLake is a unified data lake for your whole organization. Every Microsoft Fabric tenant automatically includes OneLake, and it's the single place for all your analytics data.

notes.front: What is a Fabric lakehouse?
notes.back: A Fabric item that stores structured and unstructured data in one place, managed with Delta Lake and analysed with Spark and SQL.
notes.explanation: It pairs the scale of a data lake with a warehouse’s querying, without moving data between systems.
notes.example: Like a lakehouse named “Sales” holding raw CSV exports in one folder and cleaned Delta tables in another.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?”, Overview
notes.evidence: A lakehouse in Fabric combines the scalability of a data lake with the querying capabilities of a warehouse. You store structured and unstructured data in a single location, manage it with Delta Lake, and analyze it with both Apache Spark and SQL

notes.front: What is a lakehouse’s SQL analytics endpoint?
notes.back: An endpoint Fabric generates automatically with each lakehouse, for querying its Delta tables with T-SQL.
notes.explanation: Analysts can use familiar SQL without setting up a separate warehouse.
notes.example: Like a reading-room window onto the archive: you can look up anything, but not rearrange the shelves.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?”, Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint
notes.evidence: When you create a lakehouse, Fabric automatically generates a SQL analytics endpoint. This endpoint lets you: - Query Delta tables with T-SQL — Use familiar SQL syntax without setting up a separate warehouse.

notes.front: What is Fabric Data Warehouse?
notes.back: An enterprise-scale relational warehouse built on a data lake foundation.
notes.explanation: Its relational tables sit on the lake rather than in a separate proprietary store.
notes.example: Like a traditional finance data warehouse, but whose tables are stored as open files in the company lake.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Fabric Data Warehouse?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Fabric Data Warehouse is an enterprise scale relational warehouse on a data lake foundation.

notes.front: What is Fabric Data Factory?
notes.back: The Fabric workload for connecting to data sources and moving and transforming data at scale for analytics.
notes.explanation: It gathers data scattered across databases, files, cloud services and legacy systems.
notes.example: Like a courier firm that collects parcels from many addresses, repacks them and delivers them to one depot.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Data Factory connects to more than 170 data sources, including multicloud environments and hybrid setups with on-premises gateways. It helps you move and transform your data at scale, turning it into formats that work well for analytics and decision-making.

notes.front: In Data Factory, what is a pipeline?
notes.back: A logical grouping of activities that together perform a unit of work.
notes.explanation: You manage the activities as a set rather than one by one.
notes.example: Like a recipe: fetch the ingredients, chop them, cook them, plate them, run as one job.
notes.source: Azure Data Factory documentation, “What is Azure Data Factory?”, Pipeline
notes.evidence: A pipeline is a logical grouping of activities that performs a unit of work. Together, the activities in a pipeline perform a task.

notes.front: In Data Factory, what is an activity?
notes.back: A processing step in a pipeline, such as a copy activity that copies data between data stores.
notes.explanation: There are three types: data movement, data transformation and control activities.
notes.example: Like one step in a recipe, such as “chop the onions”.
notes.source: Azure Data Factory documentation, “What is Azure Data Factory?”, Activity
notes.evidence: Activities represent a processing step in a pipeline. For example, you might use a copy activity to copy data from one data store to another data store.

notes.front: In Data Factory, what is a linked service?
notes.back: Much like a connection string: it defines the connection information needed to reach an external resource.
notes.explanation: The linked service holds the connection, while a dataset describes the structure of the data.
notes.example: Like a saved contact card with the address and door code for a supplier’s warehouse.
notes.source: Azure Data Factory documentation, “What is Azure Data Factory?”, Linked services
notes.evidence: Linked services are much like connection strings, which define the connection information that's needed for Data Factory to connect to external resources. Think of it this way: a linked service defines the connection to the data source, and a dataset represents the structure of the data.

notes.front: What is Dataflow Gen2?
notes.back: The newer Fabric dataflow: a low-code, Power Query-based tool to ingest, transform and load data without writing code.
notes.explanation: It works alongside the original dataflow, now called Gen1.
notes.example: Like cleaning a spreadsheet by clicking “remove duplicates” and “split column” instead of writing a macro.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Dataflow Gen2?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Dataflow Gen2 is the newer, more powerful version that works alongside the original Power BI Dataflow (now called Gen1). Built using the familiar Power Query experience

notes.front: What is a OneLake shortcut?
notes.back: An object in OneLake that points to another storage location, inside or outside OneLake.
notes.explanation: Shortcuts appear as folders, and any workload with access to OneLake can use them.
notes.example: Like a desktop shortcut to a file on a shared server: it opens the file where it lives.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “OneLake shortcuts”, What are shortcuts?
notes.evidence: Shortcuts are objects in OneLake that point to other storage locations. The location can be internal or external to OneLake.

notes.front: In Microsoft Fabric, what is mirroring?
notes.back: Continuous replication of existing databases and data sources into OneLake, at low cost and low latency.
notes.explanation: Once the data is in OneLake in a queryable form, every Fabric service can work with it.
notes.example: Like a live copy of a shop’s tills that head office can analyse without slowing the checkouts.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Mirroring in Fabric?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Mirroring in Fabric is a low-cost and low-latency solution that brings data from various systems together into a single analytics platform. You can continuously replicate your existing data estate directly into Fabric's OneLake from various Azure databases and external data sources.

notes.front: What is a Microsoft Fabric notebook?
notes.back: A web-based interactive surface and primary code item for developing Apache Spark jobs and machine learning experiments.
notes.explanation: Data engineers use it for ingestion, preparation and transformation code, and data scientists for machine learning.
notes.example: Like a lab notebook where each page mixes notes, code you can run and the chart it produced.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “How to use Microsoft Fabric notebooks”, Overview
notes.evidence: The Microsoft Fabric notebook is a primary code item for developing Apache Spark jobs and machine learning experiments. It's a web-based interactive surface used by data scientists and data engineers to write code benefiting from rich visualizations and Markdown text.

notes.front: What is Azure Data Factory?
notes.back: A managed cloud service for complex hybrid ETL, ELT and data integration projects.
notes.explanation: It orchestrates the processes that turn large stores of raw data into business insight.
notes.example: Like a freight scheduler that books lorries between a company’s own depots and its cloud warehouses every night.
notes.source: Azure Data Factory documentation, “What is Azure Data Factory?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Azure Data Factory is a managed cloud service that's built for these complex hybrid extract-transform-load (ETL), extract-load-transform (ELT), and data integration projects.

notes.front: What is Azure Databricks?
notes.back: A cloud analytics platform built on Apache Spark for large-scale data engineering, data science and SQL analytics.
notes.explanation: It runs as a managed service inside your Azure subscription, with Delta Lake as its native format.
notes.example: Like hiring a specialist engineering firm that brings its own Spark workshop into your premises.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Azure Databricks
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Unity Catalog in Azure Databricks?
notes.back: A unified governance layer for data and AI assets across a Databricks workspace.
notes.explanation: It provides fine-grained access control, data lineage and discovery.
notes.example: Like a building’s key register, which records who may open which room and where every item came from.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Azure Databricks
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines in Azure Databricks?
notes.back: A declarative framework for reliable, incrementally updated pipelines on Delta Lake.
notes.explanation: You describe what the output tables should hold; Databricks works out ordering, dependencies and incremental processing.
notes.example: Like telling a caterer the menu you want served and leaving the kitchen schedule to them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore data ingestion pipelines”, Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Azure Synapse Analytics?
notes.back: An enterprise analytics service that speeds insight across data warehouses and big data systems.
notes.explanation: It combines SQL for warehousing, Spark for big data, Data Explorer for logs and time series, and Pipelines for integration.
notes.example: Like one toolbox holding a SQL engine, a Spark engine and a pipeline tool, so a team needn’t assemble each piece separately.
notes.source: Azure Synapse Analytics documentation, “What is Azure Synapse Analytics?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Azure Synapse is an enterprise analytics service that accelerates time to insight across data warehouses and big data systems. Azure Synapse brings together the best of SQL technologies used in enterprise data warehousing, Spark technologies used for big data, Data Explorer for log and time series analytics, Pipelines for data integration and ETL/ELT

notes.front: What is Fabric IQ?
notes.back: A Fabric workload that provides context on the state of your business, lifting data into business language.
notes.explanation: With that context, people and agents can interpret data and decide in terms of business concepts.
notes.example: Like a shared company glossary that makes sure “customer” and “shipment” mean the same thing in every report and agent.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Fabric IQ?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Fabric IQ provides context on the state of your business. It is grounded in all the analytical, real-time, and operational data about your business, but data alone is not enough. Fabric IQ elevates that data up to the language of your business.

notes.front: In large-scale analytics architecture, what happens in the data ingestion and processing element?
notes.back: Data from sources is loaded into a data lake or data warehouse, usually by an ETL or ELT process.
notes.explanation: The data is cleaned, filtered and restructured so the result is optimised for analytical queries.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which element of large-scale analytics architecture includes data warehouses, data lakes and lakehouses?
notes.back: The analytical data store.
notes.explanation: These are the three kinds of store the training describes for large-scale analytics.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In large-scale analytics architecture, why create an analytical data model?
notes.back: To make it easier to produce reports, dashboards and interactive visualisations.
notes.explanation: Analysts could query the store directly, but a model makes reporting simpler.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In large-scale analytics architecture, what does the data visualisation element produce?
notes.back: Reports, dashboards and other visualisations built from the models and stores.
notes.explanation: It includes self-service reporting by users who are not technology professionals.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In analytics ingestion, when is data transformed in ETL, and when in ELT?
notes.back: ETL: before loading into the analytical store. ELT: after copying it into the store.
notes.explanation: Either way, the resulting structure is optimised for analytical queries.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What kind of system often performs large-scale data processing?
notes.back: Distributed systems that process high volumes in parallel on multi-node clusters.
notes.explanation: Ingestion covers both batch processing of static data and real-time processing of streaming data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Describe data warehousing architecture”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When is a data warehouse a great choice, according to the training?
notes.back: When transactional data can be organised into a structured schema of tables that you want to query with SQL.
notes.explanation: A warehouse suits data that fits cleanly into tables.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Data warehouses
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a data warehouse schema, where are numeric values commonly stored?
notes.back: In central fact tables, related to dimension tables for aggregating the data.
notes.explanation: Sales totals, for example, can then be summed by customer, product, store or time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Data warehouses
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When is a data lake a great choice, according to the training?
notes.back: For a mix of structured, semi-structured and unstructured data analysed without schema enforcement on write.
notes.explanation: Nothing constrains the files when they are stored, so varied data can land as it is.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Data lakes
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which open-source format enables data lakehouses in both Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks?
notes.back: Delta Lake.
notes.explanation: It adds relational storage capabilities on top of Parquet files.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore analytical data stores”, Hybrid approaches
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are Delta tables made of, physically?
notes.back: Parquet data files with a file-based transaction log.
notes.explanation: All Fabric data, warehouse data included, is stored this way.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Fabric Data Warehouse?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Fabric Data Warehouse data, like all Fabric data, is stored in Delta tables, which are Parquet data files with a file-based transaction log.

notes.front: Which Delta Lake benefit means partial or failed writes don’t corrupt data?
notes.back: Reliability: changes to data are tracked.
notes.explanation: Tracking changes lets the data lake behave more like a traditional database.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore Apache Spark structured streaming”, Delta Lake
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Delta Lake benefit stops messy or incompatible records from being accepted?
notes.back: Schema enforcement: data must match a defined structure first.
notes.explanation: A plain data lake, by contrast, is just a collection of files with no such check.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore Apache Spark structured streaming”, Delta Lake
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Delta Lake benefit lets one table act as both a streaming sink and a batch source?
notes.back: Unified batch and streaming.
notes.explanation: Historical and live data then need no separate storage.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore Apache Spark structured streaming”, Delta Lake
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In medallion architecture, what does the bronze layer hold?
notes.back: Raw data, stored exactly as it arrives, with no changes allowed.
notes.explanation: The original copies are preserved as a source of truth.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “Understand medallion architecture for Fabric with OneLake”, What is medallion architecture?
notes.evidence: Store everything exactly as it arrives. No changes are allowed.

notes.front: In medallion architecture, what happens to data in the silver layer?
notes.back: It is enriched: errors fixed, formats standardised and duplicates removed.
notes.explanation: Silver is the middle stage of the three-stage cleaning and organising process.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “Understand medallion architecture for Fabric with OneLake”, What is medallion architecture?
notes.evidence: Fix errors, standardize formats, and remove duplicates.

notes.front: In medallion architecture, what is the gold layer for?
notes.back: Curated data, organised for reports and dashboards.
notes.explanation: It is the highest-quality layer.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “Understand medallion architecture for Fabric with OneLake”, What is medallion architecture?
notes.evidence: Organize for reports and dashboards.

notes.front: How should the medallion layers be kept apart in Fabric?
notes.back: Each layer in its own lakehouse or warehouse in OneLake.
notes.explanation: Data moves between the layers as it is transformed and refined.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “Understand medallion architecture for Fabric with OneLake”, What is medallion architecture?
notes.evidence: Keep each layer separated in its own lakehouse or warehouse in OneLake, with data moving between the layers as it's transformed and refined.

notes.front: In which two Azure services does the training say you can use Apache Spark?
notes.back: Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks.
notes.explanation: Both include Spark runtimes with built-in Delta Lake support.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore Apache Spark structured streaming”, Overview
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How is Microsoft Fabric delivered?
notes.back: As software as a service, with OneLake as the central data lake for all workloads.
notes.explanation: Being SaaS, it needs no manual integration of separate services or management of infrastructure.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Microsoft Fabric?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Fabric is delivered as a software‑as‑a‑service (SaaS) platform and uses OneLake as a centralized, logical data lake for storing and accessing data across all workloads.

notes.front: How many OneLake instances does a Fabric tenant have?
notes.back: Exactly one; you can’t delete it or create more.
notes.explanation: There is no infrastructure to provision, and departments organise their data inside it.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is OneLake?”, Unified data storage
notes.evidence: Every Fabric tenant comes with a single OneLake instance. You can't delete OneLake or create multiple OneLakes, and there's no infrastructure to provision or manage.

notes.front: Must you copy data to use it with a different Fabric analytics engine?
notes.back: No; all Fabric engines work with the data directly in OneLake.
notes.explanation: One copy of data serves many engines without duplication.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is OneLake?”, One copy of data
notes.evidence: All Fabric analytics engines work with data directly in OneLake. You don't need to copy data to use it with another engine or analyze data from multiple sources.

notes.front: What storage service is OneLake built on, and in which open formats does it store tables?
notes.back: Azure Data Lake Storage; tables in Delta Parquet or Iceberg format.
notes.explanation: Open standards that any tool can read keep data out of proprietary formats.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is OneLake?”, Overview
notes.evidence: OneLake is built on Azure Data Lake Storage and stores tables in Delta Parquet or Iceberg format, two open standards that any tool can read.

notes.front: Which Fabric workload provides Apache Spark, with notebooks, for processing large datasets?
notes.back: Data Engineering.
notes.explanation: Its link with Data Factory lets you schedule and orchestrate notebooks and Spark jobs.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Microsoft Fabric?”, Components of Microsoft Fabric
notes.evidence: Fabric Data Engineering provides Apache Spark for processing large datasets, with notebooks and tools for writing and scheduling data transformation jobs.

notes.front: Which Fabric workload lets you build, deploy and operationalise machine learning models?
notes.back: Fabric Data Science.
notes.explanation: Analysts can then bring the predictions into their reports.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Microsoft Fabric?”, Components of Microsoft Fabric
notes.evidence: Fabric Data Science enables you to build, deploy, and operationalize machine learning models from Fabric.

notes.front: Which Fabric workload analyses data as it arrives, such as sensor readings or clickstreams?
notes.back: Real-Time Intelligence.
notes.explanation: It handles data in motion, from ingestion to real-time actions.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Microsoft Fabric?”, Components of Microsoft Fabric
notes.evidence: Real-Time Intelligence analyzes data as it arrives, such as IoT sensor readings, application logs, or website clickstreams.

notes.front: Which Fabric workload offers developer-friendly transactional databases for operational data?
notes.back: Databases.
notes.explanation: An example is SQL database in Fabric, alongside mirroring to bring other systems’ data into OneLake.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Microsoft Fabric?”, Components of Microsoft Fabric
notes.evidence: Databases in Fabric are a developer-friendly transactional database such as Azure SQL Database, which allows you to easily create your operational database in Fabric.

notes.front: Which Fabric workload separates compute from storage so each scales independently, storing data in Delta Lake format?
notes.back: Fabric Data Warehouse.
notes.explanation: The overview credits it with industry-leading SQL performance and scale.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Microsoft Fabric?”, Components of Microsoft Fabric
notes.evidence: Fabric Data Warehouse provides industry leading SQL performance and scale. It separates compute from storage, enabling independent scaling of both components. Additionally, it natively stores data in the open Delta Lake format.

notes.front: In a Fabric lakehouse, how do data engineers and analysts each typically work with the data?
notes.back: Engineers use notebooks with Spark; analysts use T-SQL.
notes.explanation: Both work on the same single copy of the data.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?”, Overview
notes.evidence: Spark and SQL access so data engineers use notebooks while analysts use T-SQL

notes.front: Can you change data through a lakehouse’s SQL analytics endpoint?
notes.back: No; it is read-only and lacks the full T-SQL surface of a warehouse.
notes.explanation: It is meant for exploration, reporting and ad-hoc queries.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?”, Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint
notes.evidence: The SQL analytics endpoint is read-only and doesn't support the full T-SQL surface of a warehouse. Use it for exploration, reporting, and ad-hoc queries.

notes.front: Which tables appear in a lakehouse’s SQL analytics endpoint?
notes.back: Only Delta tables; Parquet, CSV and other formats can’t be queried through it.
notes.explanation: A table in another format has to be converted to Delta first.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?”, Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint
notes.evidence: Only Delta tables appear in the SQL analytics endpoint.

notes.front: What are the two top-level folders of a Fabric lakehouse?
notes.back: Tables, for managed Delta tables, and Files, for unstructured or non-Delta data.
notes.explanation: Delta files placed in Tables are registered automatically so they can be queried at once.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?”, Overview
notes.evidence: A lakehouse organizes data into two top-level folders: Tables for managed Delta tables and Files for unstructured or non-Delta data.

notes.front: What are the ideal use cases for Fabric Data Warehouse?
notes.back: Star or snowflake schemas, curated corporate data marts, and governed semantic models for business intelligence.
notes.explanation: These are structured, SQL-first reporting workloads.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Fabric Data Warehouse?”, Overview
notes.evidence: The ideal use cases for Fabric Data Warehouse are star or snowflake schemas, curated corporate data marts, governed semantic models for business intelligence.

notes.front: Which Fabric tool does the training call the recommended starting point for pipeline-based ingestion?
notes.back: Fabric Data Factory, with its pipelines and Dataflows Gen2.
notes.explanation: Pipelines orchestrate multi-step workflows; dataflows give low-code transformation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, “Explore data ingestion pipelines”, Fabric Data Factory
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Does Fabric Data Factory support ETL, ELT or both?
notes.back: Both, and you can combine them in one solution.
notes.explanation: ETL suits cleaning data as it moves; ELT uses cloud-scale compute on large datasets after loading.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation, “What is Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric?”, ETL or ELT?
notes.evidence: Fabric Data Factory supports both. You can: - Build classic ETL pipelines for immediate data quality and readiness - Use ELT workflows to take advantage of integrated compute and storage for large-scale transformations - Combine both approaches in the same solution for flexibility

notes.front: How can the activities in a Data Factory pipeline run?
notes.back: Chained in sequence, or independently in parallel.
notes.explanation: The pipeline lets you manage them as a set instead of one by one.
notes.source: Azure Data Factory documentation, “What is Azure Data Factory?”, Pipeline
notes.evidence: The benefit of this is that the pipeline allows you to manage the activities as a set instead of managing each one individually. The activities in a pipeline can be chained together to operate sequentially, or they can operate independently in parallel.

notes.front: What are the three types of activity Data Factory supports?
notes.back: Data movement, data transformation and control activities.
notes.explanation: A copy activity is an example of data movement.
